newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Evergreen in deal with Chancellor.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Evergreen in deal with Chancellor.

text.p: Evergreen Media Corp and Chancellor Broadcasting agreed to merge in a stock transaction. The companies also agreed to acquire 10 radio properties from Viacom for $1.075 billion. A full text of the companies' press release follows.

EVERGREEN BROADCASTING AND CHANCELLOR BROADCASTING TO MERGE, AND TO ACQUIRE VIACOM INTERNATIONAL'S RADIO PROPERTIES, IN TRANSACTIONS CREATING AN ENTITY WITH TOTAL ENTERPRISE VALUE OF APPROXIMATELY $5 BILLION
-- Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Chairman/CEO Thomas O. Hicks Will Be Chairman of New Entity, and Evergreen Chairman/CEO Scott K. Ginsburg Will Be Its Chief Executive Officer --

IRVING, TEX., DALLAS and NEW YORK, Feb. 18, 1997 -- Evergreen Media Corporation (Nasdaq: EVGM) and Chancellor Broadcasting Company (Nasdaq: CBCA) today announced that they have entered into an agreement in principle to merge in a stock-for-stock transaction.

Evergreen and Chancellor further announced that Evergreen has signed a definitive agreement under which the combined enterprise will then acquire, for $1.075 billion, ten radio properties owned by Viacom International (AMEX: VIA, VIAB).

With an initial total of 103 radio stations in 21 major markets across the country, including stations in each of the nation's top twelve markets, with 1996 aggregate net revenues in excess of $700 million, and with a total enterprise value of approximately $5 billion, the combined enterprise will be the nation's largest pure-play radio company based on net revenues and broadcast cash flow.

The combined company will be known as Chancellor Media Corporation. Under the terms of the proposed merger agreement, Evergreen will acquire all of Chancellor Broadcasting's common stock for a fixed per share consideration of 0.9091 shares of Evergreen's Class A Common Stock.

In addition, Chancellor Media Corporation will assume Chancellor Broadcasting's obligations. After giving effect to the transaction, which is expected to be a tax-free exchange, Chancellor Media Corporation will have approximately 63 million common and common equivalent shares outstanding with current Evergreen shareholders owning approximately two-thirds, and current Chancellor Broadcasting shareholders approximately one-third, of the combined enterprise.

Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Incorporated, Steven Dinetz and Scott K. Ginsburg currently hold "super-voting" stock with ten votes per share in Chancellor Broadcasting and Evergreen, respectively. All parties will receive single-vote shares in Chancellor Media.

Separately, Evergreen and Chancellor Broadcasting also announced today that they have agreed to purchase Viacom Inc.'s entire portfolio of ten radio stations (8 FM and 2 AM) in five major markets, including Los Angeles, Chicago, New York City, Washington, D.C., and Detroit. The acquisition of the Viacom stations is subject to customary regulatory approvals and will be financed with bank credit and other traditional financing sources. Thomas O. Hicks, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Hicks Muse and Chairman of Chancellor Broadcasting, will serve as Chairman of the Board of Chancellor Media Corporation.

Scott K. Ginsburg, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer of Evergreen Media, will serve on the Board of Directors of Chancellor Media Corporation and as the Company's President and Chief Executive Officer.

Steven Dinetz and James de Castro will act as directors and co-Chief Operating Officers of Chancellor Media Corporation. Mr. Dinetz is currently President and Chief Executive Officer of Chancellor Broadcasting, and Mr. de Castro is currently President and Chief Operating Officer of Evergreen Media.
Matthew E. Devine, Evergreen's Chief Financial Officer, will serve as Chief Financial Officer of the new entity.

The Board of Directors will consist of eleven members. In addition to Messrs. Hicks, Ginsburg, Dinetz and de Castro, five independent directors will be nominated and two additional members will be nominated by Hicks Muse. The merger of Evergreen and Chancellor Broadcasting, which is subject to shareholder approval, FCC and other regulatory approvals, including expiration of the applicable Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period, and other customary closing conditions, is expected to be consummated in the third quarter of 1997.

Thomas O. Hicks, Chairman and CEO of Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst, said: "We are tremendously pleased that Chancellor Broadcasting, the radio group we formed just three years ago with Steve Dinetz, and which started out with only two radio stations in Sacramento, is now about to become part of one of the nation's very largest radio broadcasting enterprises.

The outstanding strategic, operational and financial success of Chancellor Broadcasting to date, and the company's rapid growth into its current position of industry leadership, is a tribute to the capabilities of our partner and friend Steve Dinetz, and a testament to the power of the buy-and-build philosophy with which we have built Hicks Muse itself, and so many of our portfolio companies, over the past eight years.

"We are delighted to join forces with Scott Ginsburg, Jim de Castro, and the entire Evergreen team responsible for assembling and operating an impressive portfolio of major market stations." Evergreen's Chairman, Scott K. Ginsburg, said: "Evergreen was founded nine years ago by Jim de Castro, Matt Devine and myself with six stations, three in top ten markets.

Strong station management skills and an aggressive acquisition strategy have supported the company's business plan, generating growing revenues and cash flow and the best ratings momentum in the radio industry. We have worked for many years to create an entity like Chancellor Media Corporation, which will be a powerful platform from which to operate this excellent group of radio stations. "Evergreen and Chancellor Broadcasting share a common long-term vision and entrepreneurial approach to the radio business.

We are extremely proud of Evergreen's accomplishments over the past nine years, and today's announcements cement our commitment to our employees, our advertisers and our shareholders. "I have gotten to know Tom Hicks very well, and the opportunity to bring together our acquisition, financial and operational skills will result in a radio broadcasting company which will be second to none." Robert Greenhill, Chief Executive Officer of Greenhill & Company, served as advisor to Chancellor with regard to the Viacom transaction and has rendered an opinion to Chancellor that the merger agreement between Chancellor and Evergreen is fair to Chancellor shareholders from a financial point of view.

Fred Seegal, President of Wasserstein, Perella & Co., Inc., advised Evergreen on the Viacom transaction, and Wasserstein Perella has been engaged to render an opinion to Evergreen that the merger agreement between Chancellor and Evergreen is fair to Evergreen shareholders from a financial point of view. William J. Steding, Managing Director of Star Media Group, Inc., of Dallas, originated the merger discussions between Chancellor Broadcasting and Evergreen and acted as Chancellor Broadcasting's advisor on the merger. (more) Evergreen Media Corporation, the nation's largest pure-play radio broadcasting company, currently owns or has agreements to acquire forty-two major market stations (30 FM and 12 AM) in eleven markets including Los Angeles, New York, Chicago, Dallas, San Francisco, Washington, D.C., Philadelphia, Houston, Boston, Detroit and Miami.

The Telecommunications Act of 1996 allows for the ownership of up to eight radio signals in Chicago and Philadelphia, although only five of these signals can be FM or AM; accordingly, the company will divest an FM station in each market. Since its first acquisition in January 1994, Chancellor Broadcasting has become one of the leading pure-play radio broadcasting companies in the United States. Upon consummation of all pending transactions excluding those announced today, Chancellor will own and operate 51 stations (34 FM and 17 AM) in 14 of the nation's 40 largest markets (MSAs) and six of the top ten MSAs, including New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Washington, D.C., Atlanta, Minneapolis-St. Paul, Nassau-Suffolk (Long Island, New York), Phoenix, Pittsburgh, Denver, Cincinnati, Sacramento, Orlando and Riverside-San Bernardino (California).
